How to build a page with Astryx

1. Find the page template to start from

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 build "<what you're building>"

returns: the [page] template to start from (always one: the closest match, or the app shell when nothing matches), the next two templates, and the [block]s and [component]s for the parts it lacks

2. Scaffold that template into your project

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template <name> <path>
purpose: write the page template to <path>

3. Adapt it: keep its frame and spacing, replace its content

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template <BlockName>
purpose: print a block to put inside a section, for a part the template lacks

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 component <Name>
purpose: read props before you change a component

4. Rules (keep it on-system)

- Start every page from a page template. Never lay out a page from scratch.
- Changing a page you already have? Keep it. Add blocks and components inside its sections.
- Keep the template's page frame, gap, and padding values. Replace its data, copy, and sections.
- No <div>/raw HTML for layout - use VStack/HStack/Grid/Stack/Card etc.
- No style={{}} - use component props, and design tokens for values.
- Wrap the app in <Theme theme={...}> (import {Theme} from '@astryxdesign/core/theme') and import core reset.css + astryx.css.

Related

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 template --list --type page
purpose: every page template

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 docs tokens
purpose: the design tokens

command: npx @astryxdesign/cli@0.7.12 search <query>
purpose: a neutral lookup of any component, doc, or template
